data.one_liner: Stateless widget that renders different child widgets based on screen width.
data.what_it_does: AdaptiveLayout selects a widget from small, medium, or large buckets depending on the current screen width. It uses predefined breakpoints that can be overridden globally.
use_when: Need simple responsive UI without complex state management
Want to quickly switch layouts for different screen sizes
Prefer a declarative approach to layout selection
avoid_when: Building highly dynamic layouts that change during runtime
Needing fine‑grained control over individual widget properties per breakpoint
strengths: Easy to use, single widget API
weaknesses: Only three breakpoints, no support for more granular ranges
No built‑in state management or theming integration
data.setup_notes: Add dependency, import package, use AdaptiveLayout widget

alternatives.name: responsive_framework
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides more breakpoints and responsive utilities

alternatives.name: responsive_builder
alternatives.why_pick_it: Offers a similar widget with additional helpers

data.minimal_example:
AdaptiveLayout(
  smallLayout: Container(width: 300),
  mediumLayout: Container(width: 700),
  largeLayout: Container(width: 900),
)
